CECIL M. DAGGETT — THE MAN WHO WAS TO RUN THE 1904 CAMP, IN THE BOOK CORPUS
============================================================================
Retrieved 2026-09-07 under p_430. He occurred nowhere in this project before this morning.

1. HIS OWN PUBLISHED PAPER, 1907
Source: "Educational Activities for Boys" (1907), Internet Archive educationalacti00unkngoog,
full djvu text downloaded (79,471 characters). Contents page:

    "Practical Talks — Their Operation and Secret of their Success  ....  Cecil M. Daggett"

alongside contributions by H. W. Stone, W. B. Ferris, Charles R. Scott, Robert T. Hill,
Philo R. Brooke, C. C. Robinson, I. D. Shaw and George J. Fisher. THE PAPER'S OWN BYLINE, OCR'd
"C. M. Ddw^ett, State Boys' Secretbsy, M»ine", reads:

    C. M. DAGGETT, STATE BOYS' SECRETARY, MAINE

It opens: "A careful definition of terms employed should precede a discussion upon any given
subject ... we must be absolutely sure just what Practical Talks are before we attempt to discuss
their operation or the secret of their success. In a questionnaire — that time-worn but useful
means of gathering information — recently sent to a number of boys' work directors, this question
was asked: 'What is a Practical Talk?'"

2. WHERE HE CAME FROM, from other hits in the same sweep
  "The Deke Quarterly": "Brothers CECIL M. DAGGETT, '03, and Allen Clark, '04" — Delta Kappa
      Epsilon, class of 1903.
  "The history of Colby College" (1963): "on College Sing, under Cecil M. Daggett, 1905".
  "Centennial history of The First Baptist Church of Waterville, Maine": "the Sunday School
      Superintendent, Mr. Cecil M. Daggett".
COLBY COLLEGE IS AT WATERVILLE, MAINE. He is a Colby man of the class of 1903, and the church and
the state secretaryship are both in his own town and state.

3. WHY IT FITS MONTREAL EXACTLY
Men of Montreal, June 1904: "The camp will be in charge of Mr. C. M. Daggett." The 1904 issue
also has him arriving: "Last May Mr. R. H. Macdonald left the work, and during the summer months
we were without a Secretary. IN SEPTEMBER MR. C. M. DAGGETT CAME AND TOOK CHARGE." The 1905
annual report has him going: "MR. C. M. DAGGETT LEFT IN MAY to take the Junior Secretaryship of
the ST. LOUIS, MO., ASSOCIATION."
SO: COLBY 1903 -> MONTREAL THAT SEPTEMBER -> the 1904 camp -> St. Louis in May 1905 -> State
Boys' Secretary for Maine by 1907, back in his own state.

THE PATTERN THIS MAKES WITH HOLLINSHEAD, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING PART
Kenneth J. Hollinshead: ALBION COLLEGE, CLASS OF 1910 -> Montreal's Boys' Secretaryship the same
year, at twenty-three (f_5329).
Cecil M. Daggett: COLBY COLLEGE, CLASS OF 1903 -> Montreal's boys' work that September.
TWICE, SEVEN YEARS APART, THE YMCA OF MONTREAL TOOK ITS BOYS' SECRETARY STRAIGHT OUT OF AN
AMERICAN COLLEGE — and the office it was hiring for is the one that ran the camp. Two cases is a
pattern worth testing, not a practice established; the men between them are Maclaren, Holliday
and Brooks, whose entries into Association work are 04, 06 and 05.
